expected_symptom: Compiling the filed ByteAddressBuffer.Load(X) shader with an uninitialized index X succeeds silently (exit 0): no front-end diagnostic by default, and the bundled DXIL validator does not flag the resulting i32 undef, i32 undef bufferLoad operands. Per damyanp's 2024-08-27 comment the issue is now scoped to the validator gap, not the (already-answered) front-end-default-warning question.
history: always-repro'd across v1.4.1907..v1.9.2607 (full --linear scan, 20/20 probeable stable releases; 5 prereleases excluded by policy); reproduces on main-debug and on CE dxc_1_6_2112/dxc_trunk
reviewed_by: gpt-5.3-codex (independent batch-019 step-10 review; applied selectively at collation)
summary: Still reproduces on main-debug (89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df): the filed repro (ByteAddressBuffer.Load of an uninitialized uint index, ps_6_0) compiles cleanly, exit 0, with no diagnostic and DXIL keeping the buffer-load index as i32 undef, i32 undef (both coordinate operands) -- matching the issue body's quoted line exactly. The default (non-Vd) DXIL validator does not flag it either, confirming @damyanp's 2024-08-27 re-scoping of the issue onto the validator. -Wuninitialized still catches it (spot-checking @llvm-beanz's 2023 comment) but remains off by default, a deliberate policy choice (not re-litigated here) tied to closed issues #2494/#5377. bisect --linear: all 20 probeable stable releases from v1.4.1907 through v1.9.2607 reproduce (5 prereleases excluded by policy) -- always-repro'd, not a regression. Controls: an initialized-index variant does not match (proving the fully-undef anchor is not vacuous, since ByteAddressBuffer.Load's second bufferLoad coordinate is always undef regardless of the bug), and adding -Wuninitialized flips the absence clause as expected. Compiler Explorer (dxc_1_6_2112 + dxc_trunk) corroborates: identical undef shape, no diagnostic on either pane.
title: Undefined value allowed for buffer load index
